question: the mac (b07b445) asks why the preprocessed profile at truth a = 0.25 um puts the best fit 39.7 log-likelihood above the truth, and proposes that the rubberband lifts noisy data by ~2 sigma

rubberband_lift.definition: mean of the rubberband-corrected 1600-1700 window, noisy data minus the same quantity for the noise-free model
rubberband_lift.verdict: confirmed: +2.09 sigma, as the mac predicted. The rubberband anchors on noise minima, so correcting noisy data lifts the window while the noise-free model is not lifted. At a = 0.25 um that bias is 58 % of the Amide I band depth, which is why the truth fits badly.

chi2_of_the_truth_model_against_its_own_.verdict: the pre-registered preprocessed likelihood is misspecified by about 2x in chi^2 even at the truth: 99.7 against 52 data points. A free scale plus a free CONSTANT fixes it outright (49.2, against 50 expected for 52 - 2). Adding the slope term buys 1.5 more chi^2 for one more parameter, i.e. nothing. So s*m + c0 is sufficient; c1*(nu-1650) is optional and may still be wanted for real data.
